chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ali ibn Abi Hamza from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the child is not valid, nor is the divorce of the intoxicated one.
ai.seo_question: Is divorce valid for a child or an intoxicated person in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes that divorce is invalid for a young child and an intoxicated person due to their lack of full mental capacity (ahl al-talaq). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the necessity of *rushd* (sound judgment) and consciousness for the validity of legal acts, distinguishing between mere minority and the specific impairment of intoxication.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Ali Bin Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The divorce of the child is not allowed, nor of the intoxicated ones’.
en.sarwar: 3. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from Ali ibn abu Hamzah from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Divorce by a child and one who is drunk do not have any valid effect.’”
